newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Kvaerner H1 profits disappoint.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Kvaerner H1 profits disappoint.

text.p: Shares in engineering and construction group Kvaerner ASA fell sharply on Tuesday after the Anglo-Norwegian company reported a disappointing 19 percent first-half profit rise.

Kvaerner, which has its headquarters in London but is listed on the Oslo stock exchange, said pre-tax profit rose to 840 million Norwegian crowns ($109.9 million) from 706 million, coming in well below market forecasts.
As a result, Kvaerner A shares closed down 27 crowns, or 5.8 percent, to 431 crowns.
"Most analysts will adjust their (profit) margin estimates down. Revenues are okay, but Kvaerner is not yet able to earn good money," an analyst said.
Group sales rose sharply, largely reflecting the contribution of Britain's Trafalgar House group of companies bought in April 1996 for $1.37 billion.
Kvaerner said results were still not satisfactory, but repeated its forecast of much better full-year operating profits as market conditions continued to improve amid further restructuring efforts.
Kvaerner's ship building operations -- the group's main money maker -- saw profits decline to 525 million crowns from 545 million.
President and chief executive Erik Tonseth said the business' outlook was, however, good as fierce competition had forced rivals to close down.
"Competition is changing and we are in a very comfortable position," Tonseth said.
He also predicted strong growth in the oil and gas business, which among others makes drilling platforms.
An organisational restructuring would help the sector overcome a poor first-half performance in Norway, Tonseth added.
He also saw scope for big orders in Asia which would help Kvaerner's process technology sector after it already saw first-half pre-tax profit increase tenfold.
"We believe that process technology and oil and gas can show substantial progress," he told reporters.
Results in the languishing pulp and paper business continued to pick up, with losses for the half year narrowing to 27 million crowns from 133 million.
Tonseth said pulp prices appeared to be on the increase and said the sector would benefit from further cost cutting measures.
He predicted a full-year break-even result for the construction business after unspecified problems with contracts in the United States, inherited from Trafalgar House, were solved.
Speaking for the group as a whole, Tonseth said: "We feel things are going in the right direction."
